title: Robotic assisted versus manually instrumented total knee revision arthroplasty- a randomized, controlled trial
summary: The aim of this study is to measure (1) radiologic results, (2) patient satisfaction and (3) complications after robotic-assisted versus manually instrumented total knee revision arthroplasty. In a robotic-assisted knee revision arthroplasty, the surgeon relies on a robotic system to aid in the positioning of the implants, in a manual instrumentation, this is done with alignment rods.
conditions: Mechanical complication after total knee arthroplasty

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written consent for participation in the study
Planned single stage total knee arthroplasty revision using a non-hinged implant type
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who did not consent to participate
Patients who are not able to consent because of mental disabilities or lack or a language barrier
Revision due to a tumor or infection
Revision to a hinged-type implant
